newsitem.title: UK: LME aluminium still tight, nearby premiums high.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium still tight, nearby premiums high.

text.p: Tightness in the aluminium market continued during Tuesday LME ring and kerb trading, with premiums for very prompt metal flaring considerably.

In active trading, the premium to borrow "tom/next" metal (belated business against the previous day's prompt date) leapt to $21 as shorts were forced to cover. On Monday, cash/one day was at $5 when it was trading as the "third Wednesday".

Cash/one day traded at $12 backwardation today, cash/one week was near $30, while the cash/threes spread was $45/48. Much of the tightness has been rolled forward to September, which is likely to be the focus of attention as the squeeze continues.

LME authorities monitored the dealings this morning without taking any action. "The August date was the key date in aluminium, so we're watching how it performed," LME Chief Executive David King said.
Some traders voiced concern over the level of the premium for "tom/next" - this was the August date from Monday's cash.
"The LME has a one percent limit in copper (on the daily backwardation), so why not aluminium," one said.
The copper limit is one percent of the previous day's cash price. In aluminium, if imposed, daily backwardations would have a ceiling of $17.

The forward market was softer - a reflection of the general tone - but was partially cushioned by an unexpected 425-tonne stock fall. But this is likely to be a one-off, as sizeable stock increases in coming days are expected, traders said.
Last three months trade was at $1,664, down $13 from Monday's kerb close.

Elsewhere, a mostly softer tone prevailed in the complex, highlighted by lower copper and zinc markets. The red metal managed to hold above Monday's late 7-1/2 month lows of $2,135, but has little incentive on the upside.

Stocks rose 4,075 tonnes, while there was also some lending against the forward spreads which are still in backwardation. The wider cash/threes spread was maintained at $3/6 contango, while last three months business was at $2,142, down $20.
Zinc also fell back, despite a 5,175 tonne drop in stocks, with the September tightness seen keeping the market volatile and uncertain. Last trade was $17 lower at $1,475.

Nickel continued to stage a modest correction to recent steep declines, but appeared limited on the upside, with stocks rising and many expecting a resolution to the Falconbridge dispute soon. Last business was $50 higher at $6,720.
Tin also edged up, aided by a 120-tonne stock fall, and was $20 higher at $5,390. However, lead drifted lower, and was down $3 at $607. Alloy was stable at $1,500/10.
